I'm requesting changes. The chunking of long words and the empty-text check look fine, and they match the docstring. The switch from `<=` to `<` in the line-filling check is the problem.

By the agent's own account in the PR description, that change exists only so `test_meeting_reminder` passes. It contradicts the docstring, which says lines are "at most width characters", and you said the docstrings are the source of truth.

It also leaves the function inconsistent. A lone word or chunk can still be exactly `width` characters, but a line with several words now tops out at `width - 1`. Callers get an off-by-one that depends on the input.

The agent was upfront about this, which helps, but the fix isn't mergeable as written. Since the test and the docstring disagree and tests can't be changed, this needs a decision from you or whoever owns `wrap.py`: either the test's expected value is wrong, or the docstring is out of date. Please revert the `<` change, keep the chunking and empty-text fixes, and raise the conflict so someone decides which one to correct.
